name: Arkab Posterior
description: A star 41 parsecs away, 4.1 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 95294: radius 4.106 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 28.998 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.12) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 95294: effective temperature 6615 +/- 451 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.171)

gravity.source: SIMBAD's compilation of spectroscopic measurements (mesFe_h): log g 3.55 from 2003A&A...398.1121E; the 1 published value span log g 3.55 to 3.55, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.0% of the centre brightness

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 95294: distance 41.135 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.008), at which the luminosity and radius hold

text.card: A star 41 parsecs away, 4.1 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 29 times the Sun's luminosity at 6,615 K, so 4.106 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 95294: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: Beta2 Sagittarii
quotes.card: Beta2 Sagittarii is a star in the southern zodiac constellation of Sagittarius.
quotes.introduction: It is visible to the naked eye, having an apparent visual magnitude of +4.29.
